s: Inseparable verbal prefix indicating privation or the direction of 'forth', 'away'.
Inseparable verbal prefix that denotes a transition of the object into a state, which is indicated by the stem.
ver- + lieben (“to love”) → sich verlieben (“to fall in love”)
ver- + urteilen (“to pronounce judgement”) → verurteilen (“to convict”)
Inseparable verbal prefix for forming verbs out of adjectives, indicating a change towards that quality.
ver- + schöner (“more beautiful”) + -n → verschönern (“to beautify, to make prettier”)
Inseparable verbal prefix indicating a faulty action, often as a reflexive verb.
ver- + laufen (“to walk”) → sich verlaufen (“to get lost”)
ver- + zählen (“to count”) → sich verzählen (“to miscount”)
Inseparable verbal prefix that denotes losing something (money, resources etc.) by way of doing something indicated by the stem. In this sense, the opposite to er-.
ver- + zocken (“to gamble”) → verzocken (“to lose by gambling”)
ver-.et: From Middle High German ver-, from Old High German far-, fir-, from Proto-West Germanic *fra-, from a mixture of Proto-Germanic *firi- (expresses intensive or perfective meaning), *fra- (“forth, away, off; fully, completely, up”), *furi- (“against, opposed”) a…
